fieldissues.issue: The descriptions claim more than 800 February layoffs and more than 1,000 March layoffs, while the retained AP source note summarizes two rounds of roughly 500 and 800 cuts. The exact counts and timing do not align within the supplied source metadata.
The short repeats a title that says NOAA was “gutted” and research programs were “dismantled”; the long also uses “devastated” and includes an unformatted direct quotation from Tom Di Liberto.

proposedchanges.change: Resolve the layoff counts and rounds against the reporting before retaining the exact totals. If the record keeps additional laboratory and balloon-launch effects, retain sources that document those specific outcomes.

After the counts are resolved, use a neutral title that describes the reported workforce reductions and affected NOAA services. Write a separate short and format Tom Di Liberto’s warning as an attributed quotation or paraphrase.

evidencebasis: The assignment’s AP source note describes roughly 500 and 800 cuts in two rounds, while the merged long says more than 800 in February and more than 1,000 in March.
The merged title and short repeat each other and use “gutted” and “dismantled”; the only retained URL is AP.
The long introduces Tom Di Liberto’s words with a colon but does not mark them as a quotation.
notes: The count discrepancy and the scope of the reported operational impacts need source alignment before the headline and summary can be finalized.

fieldissues.issue: The long extends from the water-restoration and hydrant claims to FEMA funding, a billionaire couple hoarding water, handbag firefighting equipment, and arson allegations, but the sole retained FactCheck.org URL and its support note cover the water claims and rebuttals.
The title repeats as the short and says Trump blamed Newsom for “sabotaging” the wildfires, a stronger formulation than the medium’s water-policy claims.

proposedchanges.change: Add sources for the FEMA funding, water-hoarding, handbag-equipment, and arson claims if they remain. Otherwise narrow the account to the nonexistent water declaration and the water-policy claims covered by FactCheck.org.

Use a title such as “FactCheck.org Examines Trump’s Claims About Water and the Los Angeles Fires.” Write a distinct short that attributes his claims and the state and expert responses without saying he proved or caused wildfire sabotage.

evidencebasis: The source metadata identifies FactCheck.org’s report on the water declaration and hydrant claims as the retained source.
The merged long adds multiple separate claims about FEMA funding, hoarding, handbags, and arson that are not identified in that source note.
The merged title and short are identical, and “sabotaging” exceeds the medium’s specific description of Trump’s claims.
notes: The water-policy fact-check is supported by the retained URL. The additional claims need their own source links or removal.

Attribute criticism of the subpoenas and the department’s legal process to the judge, journalists, or other named sources. Distinguish subpoenas to reporters from carrier requests covering relatives’ phone records.

The AP source URL from the packet remains in source_urls.
notes: The central event is well described, but the headline changes who received subpoenas and the long should attribute its judgments.

fieldissues.issue: The long asserts the rule change delivered a direct win to Nexstar and Sinclair, gives their pending deals and political support, and describes a pattern of investigations and favorable treatment. Use a title that describes the FCC vote without saying the deals were cleared or labeling the companies politically aligned. Write a distinct short that distinguishes a rule change from later merger decisions.

evidencebasis: The packet’s Washington Post source note and merged source_urls identify one article about the 2–1 vote and replacement process.
The merged medium says the rule change could affect proposed acquisitions; the long says it delivered a direct win and alleges a broader pattern.
The merged short repeats the title and elevates possible effects into a completed path for consolidation.
notes: The source supports the rule change, but the wider claims about individual companies and other FCC matters need corresponding sources or narrower scope.
